Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

plunder verb

also sack, pillage, loot, ransack, tear apart, lay waste

classical

Caes. BG 7.8.4: ab hostibus dīripī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 2.17.2: impedīmentīs dīreptīs (Lewis & Short)

dīripiō, dīripere, dīripuī, dīreptum

verb, third conjugation

tear apart; of an enemy’s land or goods, lay waste, plunder, sack

Other words

  • vāstō, vāstāre, vāstāvī, vāstātum — make empty, leave desolate; lay waste, ravage

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 3.32.2: vāstātī agrī sunt (Lewis & Short); Cic. ND 2.99 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • impedīmentīs dīreptīs

    the baggage having been plunderedCaes. BG 2.17.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • quī puerīs in epilogum prōductīs tālōs jēcit in medium, quōs illī dīripere coepērunt

    who, when the children had been brought on for the peroration, threw knucklebones into the middle, and they began to scramble for themQuint. 6.1.47

  • vāstātī agrī sunt

    the fields were laid wasteLiv. 3.32.2 (Lewis & Short)

See also rob, spoils.
